column5: K_S - the Monod- or saturation constant - is the concentration of substrate A at which the rate equals half of its maximum value, r_m.
r_m is the maximum specific rate of biomass growth, i.e., the rate when the substrate concentration is not limiting (C_A much larger than K_S)
In the original Monod equation, r is represented by mu, r_m by mu_max and C_A by S. Also, mu is called the growth rate constant, with dimension h-1.
the empirical Monod-kinetics, which are shaped after the Michaelis-Menten kinetics for enzymatic reactions
In this case r, when plotted versus the substrate concentration, exhibits a maximum, whereas with Monod-kinetics it tends to an asymptotic value.
